thread: Cllr George Carroll (Llandough ward member) — correspondence with no reply
subject: Great House Farm/ Church View Close
body:
Cllr Carroll,

I hope this email finds you well.

I am writing to follow up on my previous emails regarding matters connected
to Great House Farm / Church View Close in Llandough. Although I am not
currently a resident, my family has deep historical roots in the area since
1667 and we maintain a legitimate interest in the land, history, and
related issues.

For your reference, here is a summary of my prior correspondence to you:
Email Date Key Points Raised
16 Feb 2026 • Potential gaps in Council planning and record-keeping for
Great House Farm (demolished 1988) • Title fraud and procedural concealment
relating to Church View Close (formerly Great House Farm / Ty Mawr)
4 May 2026 • Setting aside BP vs Buckler 1987 case (stolen paper title,
identity fraud, court mistakes, procedural unfairness) • Shared ITV footage
link and request for attention as Llandough Councillor
7 Jun 2026 • Church View Close, Llandough – piecing together 1988 events
from public records, family testimony, and media
25 Jun 2026 • Enquiry whether you had reviewed prior concerns on family
dispossession from land in Llandough; request for any progress or discussion

I'd also like to know who removed the tree my great grandad planted to
commemorate our ownership claim. As per the image in the collection of
Wales archive.

I have not received substantive replies to these points. As the elected
Councillor for Llandough, you have a public duty to respond to reasonable
enquiries from those with a legitimate interest in the ward in a timely
manner (typically within 10–15 working days per standard local authority
expectations).

I would appreciate your detailed response to the above at your earliest
convenience, ideally within the next 10 working days.

Thank you for your attention. I look forward to your reply.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

thread: Cllr George Carroll (Llandough ward member) — correspondence with no reply
subject: Great House Farm, Llandough
body:
George,

Have you had an opportunity to look into any of the concerns I have raised
with you regarding my family's dispossession from land at Llandough?

Might we be able to achieve even the smallest task together in trying to
unravel what I allege may have involved fraud, concealment, mistakes, or
other wrongdoing surrounding my family's loss of possession of land there?

It is land that my family claimed to own, and that claim has never, to my
knowledge, been extinguished or determined against us by a court.

The possibility of errors relating to my grandmother's and father's deaths,
court mistakes, Land Registry mistakes, the dismissal of my father's appeal
against the 1987 ruling, the rejection of the ECHR application, and Cadw's
inaction do not alter the central point: my family's claim to ownership of
the land itself has never been properly adjudicated upon or defeated.

I may even have an interest in Church View Close. I am raising concerns
about what could amount to a major scandal in the manner in which my family
and I were dispossessed of land there. Your lack of response, together with
a number of unusual or contradictory responses I have received from other
parties connected with the matter, has not reassured me that there is a
willingness to examine these issues openly.

If evidence was destroyed, if mistakes were made, or if fraud or
concealment occurred, I am sure you would prefer to assist in establishing
the truth rather than be perceived as defending or perpetuating any
wrongdoing.

Would you at least be willing to help with the more limited task of
identifying when the tree planted by my family was removed? From what I can
gather, the tree planting commemorated our claim to absolute title over our
plot of land. Its removal could arguably represent the destruction of
evidence connected with that claim.

Regards,

Sion Buckler
Retired Sergeant

thread: FOI/EIR 00211027 — acquisition of land for Llandough Primary School
subject: Request for information regarding acquisition of land for Llandough Primary School
body:
Sirs/ Ma'am,

Under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and, where applicable, the
Environmental Information Regulations 2004, I request copies of records
relating to the acquisition of the land used for the construction of
Llandough Primary School.

Specifically, I request:

■ The transfer deed, conveyance or other legal instrument by which the
Council acquired the land.

■ The purchase price or consideration paid for the land.

■ If the land was gifted, transferred at nominal value or below market
value, records explaining the basis for that arrangement.

■ Any valuation reports obtained before acquisition.

■ Any agreements, correspondence or meeting minutes between the Council and
BP (or any BP subsidiary, trust or associated company) concerning the
transfer of the land.

■ Any Cabinet, Committee or Council reports authorising the acquisition.

■ Any planning agreements or obligations connected with the transfer.

If any of the requested information is already publicly available, please
provide the relevant links or document references.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
[redacted]
02031377118
